body:
Using player.getTotalBufferedDuration() I manage to understand how this issue is be produce.

we are playing a live stream that has as base this values

	#EXT-X-TARGETDURATION:6
	#EXTINF:4.166,live
	#EXTINF:2.000,live
	#EXTINF:1.084,live

the rule for **#EXT-X-TARGETDURATION** says that all Media Segments will be less or equal to defined value so is not a problem that the TARGETDURATION = 6 and EXTINF lower then that;

The value for **TARGETDURATION** never changes, the playback starts the value for **player.getTotalBufferedDuration()** stays at 6 to 7s for about 10s of playback (setBufferDurationsMs is allowing the value to go above this it can't because is live content), after this initial 10s the **player.getTotalBufferedDuration()** stars to get lower, lower than 6s,
[loadPlaylist()](https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/blob/dev-v2/library/hls/src/main/java/com/google/android/exoplayer2/source/hls/playlist/DefaultHlsPlaylistTracker.java#L492) is triggered but the segments loaded aren't enough to fill the 6s duration of TARGETDURATION, the **player.getTotalBufferedDuration()** get higher but is less than 6s, the buffers keeps going down and down until it reaches 0, at this point **loadPlaylist()** already triggered again but is too late Player.STATE_BUFFERING already trigger the playback has stopped and when the segments are available again the **player.getTotalBufferedDuration()** may go above 6s or not and stay like this for some time, until eventually goes above 6s stays like that for some time but eventually will drop and the issue shows up again and again, can take minutes to happen sometimes but it does all the time.

Keep the value **targetDurationUs = 1s** prevent this from ever happen, but causes unnecessary loadPlaylist() calls every 1s in the case TS are only be created at a 2s rate for example.

So the scenario that probably can occurs to any live stream where at some point has a amount of segments with they added duration time is almost equal or less than targetDurationUs we have this issue.

The first thing that comes to mind is not only call **loadPlaylist()** on the situation that **targetDurationUs** demands but also on the situation that the buffer has already consume all the segments available, not constantly all the time to prevent a race, but at the time the segments are all consumed, and then again in 1s or so if the server didn't provide enough on last update call.

Take a look here and see what can be done, I think I provide enough info about the issue, if need test or more info let me know.
@AquilesCanta Can you please comment on this issue?

> this means that we can't restrict the load of a new playlist base on this value

The HLS specification explicitly says that clients must do this, at least under some circumstances:

> If the client reloads a Playlist file and finds that it has not changed then it MUST wait for a period of one-half the target duration before retrying.

To me, this implies that segment durations probably shouldn't be less than one-half of the target duration either, where-as in the snippet above it seems that segment durations are much shorter.

> To me, this implies that segment durations probably shouldn't be less than one-half of the target duration either, where-as in the snippet above it seems that segment durations are much shorter.

If  the below is a rule
> Media Segments will be less or equal to EXT-X-TARGETDURATION

exo should account for it and not expected they be bigger then half.

this:
https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/blob/dev-v2/library/hls/src/main/java/com/google/android/exoplayer2/source/hls/playlist/DefaultHlsPlaylistTracker.java#L657

is never be used on this issue I have checked is not a problem of empty/unchanged playlist.

The issue is that exo doesn't account that it can load segments that will not fill up the **targetDurationUs** and base the next playlist load only on that.

I have be playing this same playlist for years now (on non android devices) and never had a issue on any player, I only start to see it when using exoplayer, so others players account for this as is expected...

They do the time verification for next playlist call based on the duration of the already visible segments without expecting those be equal to EXT-X-TARGETDURATION or at least some relation of it.

rename.from: HSL Live stream targetDurationUs is not always a ideal way to calculate time for next playlist load
rename.to: HLS Live stream targetDurationUs is not always a ideal way to calculate time for next playlist load

body:
I'm not sure I understand your response. The HLS specification states:

> When a client loads a Playlist file for the first time or reloads a
> Playlist file and finds that it has changed since the last time it
> was loaded, the client MUST wait for at least the target duration
> before attempting to reload the Playlist file again, measured from
> the last time the client began loading the Playlist file.
>
> If the client reloads a Playlist file and finds that it has not
> changed, then it MUST wait for a period of one-half the target
> duration before retrying.

The code you reference appears to do exactly that, in which case we're implementing the specification correctly. Conversely, you appear to be saying that we should implement something that's explicitly not what the HLS specification asks for. Please clarify.

from where you are reading those specification? share the link please.

tell me if this is also a " HLS specification"

> Media Segments will be less or equal to EXT-X-TARGETDURATION

if it is and is be used here so I guess yes, there is the chance that you load a playlist that has on it segments that they total time is less then **EXT-X-TARGETDURATION**, in that case the next playlist can't be load base on **EXT-X-TARGETDURATION** alone, because if that happens this issue I open will happens.

So if "Media Segments will be less or equal to EXT-X-TARGETDURATION" is a rule, the way exo loads playlist can't be used as it directly conflict on how the total time of this new playlist can be.

so does exoplayer account for the total time of the segments loaded be less then next TARGETDURATION?
NO

can it do?
YES

So do you understand the issue now?

can it be fixed and all the rules even those that conflict be addressed?

> from where you are reading those specification? share the link please.

The same specification that you've already linked to. [Section 6.3.4](https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-pantos-http-live-streaming-23#section-6.3.4).

> the next playlist can't be load base on EXT-X-TARGETDURATION alone

The specification is very clear about the minimum delay between playlist refreshes, and your proposal explicitly goes below them. It's unlikely that this is correct.

> there is the chance that you load a playlist that has on it segments that they total time is less then EXT-X-TARGETDURATION, in that case the next playlist can't be load base on EXT-X-TARGETDURATION alone, because if that happens this issue I open will happens.

On further thought, I don't think this is correct. Provided the playback position isn't too close to the live edge, the segments can be arbitrarily short and playback should work fine with the current playlist refresh behaviour. You'll just see more than one new segment each time the playlist is refreshed, which is fine. Are you doing anything special to get the playback position closer to the live edge than it is by default? Is the initial playback position closer to the live edge than it is for other players?

No I'm not, I notice that the playback is as close to the edge as can be, the only thing I have change is that the default buffers are lower DEFAULT_BUFFER_FOR_PLAYBACK_MS and DEFAULT_BUFFER_FOR_PLAYBACK_AFTER_REBUFFER_MS are 1s.

When the **HlsMediaPlaylist** is called the total segment size is 28s, but it isn't starting on the first segment but 6s before the end.

With is odd as that is the **targetDurationUs** size, here is very noticeable, I start the playback player.getTotalBufferedDuration() goes to 6 and starts to drop, reaches 0, loadPlaylist() is called loades more 6s and stay like this, the problem is that it does not do fast enough so **Player.STATE_BUFFERING** is always triggered and playback stops every 6s after the issue starts.

What in exoplayer could cause this behavior?

Exo see that there is 28s of segments but start at the last 6s (targetDurationUs = 6), and because of that the issue is display.

The player other than the default buffer sizes changes, I start with

	player.prepare(mediaSource, true, true);

No seek or anything related before that is called for live content...

I think there are two different topics in discussion here:
- Quick rebuffer after starting playback.
- Playlist reloading policy.

On the quick rebuffer topic:

> playback starts 6s to the live-edge.

ExoPlayer's default start position for live playback is 3 segments from the live edge. In your case, your last 3 segments' total duration is 6 seconds. The target duration is 6 seconds, so we won't reload the playlist for 6 seconds, time after which the buffer will surely be exhausted. **Note**: After some rebuffering, playback should stabilize unless the window is 3 segments long (please don't do that, may be worth reading [this post](https://medium.com/google-exoplayer/hls-playback-in-exoplayer-a33959a47be7)).

There are two ways of fixing this, as far as I can see:
- You can set an [EXT-X-START](https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-pantos-http-live-streaming-23#section-4.3.5.2) of -12 (means playback will start 12 seconds from the live edge).
- You can implement your own playlist tracker that reloads the media playlist as you see fit.

On the playlist reloading policy: 
The standard is pretty clear about how to reload media playlists. I doubt we should adjust it for specific cases, since we might create issues for others (for example, by DOSing).

By the way, nice chimarrão.

Agreed the policy about playlist reloading is clear. Given this, we should probably change our default start position to better handle cases where segments are significantly shorter than the target duration. For example:

1. Start at least 3 segments back from the live edge (this is the current rule)
1. Also start at least 2 (or 3?) target durations back from the live edge (this would be an additional rule to handle cases such as the one in this issue)

What do you think?

So I check and most stream I tested before the TS was 2s so the 6s issue comes from this edge position and target duration be equal, as when was a bigger TS I didn't notice the issue, but those TS size are rare.

> * Start at least 3 segments back from the live edge (this is the current rule)
> * Also start at least 2 (or 3?) target durations back from the live edge (this would be an additional rule to handle cases such as the one in this issue)

This seems OK, maybe a simple check **if (3 segments size <= target durations) starting point = 3 segments size + target durations;**

Also check if there is that much segments in time if not start on the first one (maybe the code already does that).
I know you guys know how to deal with that logic, just a idea.

We can change the default start duration to start from 

```
Math.min(
    segments.isEmpty()
        ? 0
        : segments.get(Math.max(0, segments.size() - 3)).relativeStartTimeUs,
    playlist.durationUs - playlist.targetDurationUs * 2);
```
Using 2 will keep the existing behavior for most users while reducing the risk of entering buffering state. If we want to use 3 * target duration we can just remove the old behavior.

Note @fgl27 that you should set the default start position in the playlist as suggested above . That way you can guarantee a consistent playback experience across all platforms.

That worked, **player.getTotalBufferedDuration()** is now oscillating from 5 to 12s, no rebuffers call, I can see the playlist update it 6s as expected, all is just fine.
